OpenLog Contact

OpenLog / Privacy Policy

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 November 2026 · Draft for legal review

This policy describes how the OpenLog app and website handle information.

Review notice. The code does not show whether production analytics are active, how long PostHog keeps data, which legal entity operates OpenLog, or which age groups and countries OpenLog serves. Resolve the owner questions in docs/privacy-audit.md before publication.

How OpenLog works

OpenLog does not require an account and does not provide cloud sync. It stores your timeline in app storage on your device. The app does not send the full timeline or its attachments to an OpenLog server as a feature. Some services receive limited information, as described below.

Information stored on your device

OpenLog stores information that you add or choose:

  • Entry text, dates and times, tags, and locations that you add.
  • Location coordinates and the place label returned by the device geocoder.
  • Photos, voice recordings, other files, and their names, types, and sizes.
  • Your optional profile name and app preferences.
  • Unsaved drafts, which can include text, media, tags, dates, and locations.

OpenLog uses these data to create, search, and display entries, save drafts, and apply your preferences. Search runs in the local database. The app copies selected media into its local storage.

OpenLog does not remove metadata from every attachment. Some photos stay as original files. They can contain information such as capture time or location.

Analytics and error reports

Some non-development app builds send analytics to PostHog when the build includes the PostHog project token. The code does not show whether the production build includes that token. OpenLog has no in-app control to turn analytics off.

Product events can record:

  • Screen names and app install, update, open, active, and background events.
  • Entry creation, update, or deletion, plus whether an entry has text or a location.
  • Counts of attached photos, recordings, and files.
  • Recording duration, backup entry count, and backup file size.
  • Location use, app-lock changes, and the notification permission choice.

These event fields do not include entry text, media files, attachment names, or exact location coordinates. The app sends a persistent pseudonymous installation identifier. It does not send your profile name or call PostHog's user-identification method.

The PostHog SDK also sends app version and build, device model and manufacturer, operating system and version, locale, time zone, screen size, and the app environment. The PostHog service receives the network request IP address. The app does not disable PostHog's IP-based location estimate, so PostHog can infer an approximate region from that address, subject to project settings. Events go to PostHog's US endpoint.

An app-open event can include the launch URL supplied by the operating system. The SDK also captures unhandled JavaScript errors, rejected promises, and errors from an app error boundary. Error reports can include error messages and stack traces. The app redacts file paths from errors sent through its manual reporting helper. Automatic error reports do not use that helper. An error message or launch URL can contain personal information.

The app disables interaction autocapture, session replay, and console capture. The code does not set a PostHog data-retention period. PostHog's privacy policy and project settings govern its handling and retention.

Location

OpenLog requests foreground location only when you ask to add or refresh a place. It sends the coordinates to the native geocoding service to get a place label. iOS uses Apple's Core Location geocoder. Android uses the Android Geocoder API. The code does not name a fixed downstream provider for Android. These services can receive your coordinates.

OpenLog saves the coordinates and returned place label in the draft or entry on your device. It does not track location in the background. Analytics record whether you used location, not the coordinates or place label.

Fonts and the website

If you select an optional font that is not cached, OpenLog downloads it from the jsDelivr CDN and stores it on your device. The request identifies the font file and sends ordinary network data, such as your IP address. It does not include entry content.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The website stylesheet requests fonts from Google Fonts. GitHub and Google receive website and font requests with ordinary connection data. The website source contains no analytics script or cookie-based tracking code. The repository does not show the hosting providers' log or cookie practices.

The website links to external services. If you open one, that service handles your visit under its own privacy terms.

Permissions and notifications

OpenLog requests access when you use these features:

  • Photo-library access when you choose images to attach.
  • Microphone access when you start a recording.
  • Foreground location access when you ask to add or refresh a place.
  • File access through the device file picker when you choose an attachment or backup.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after you first reach the timeline. If you allow it, the app creates local notifications for backup and import progress. A completion notice can show the entry count and backup file size. The device can show these notices on its lock screen, subject to your notification settings. The code does not register a remote push-notification token.

Backups and sharing

When you export a backup, OpenLog creates a compressed archive with your entries, tags, settings, locations, attachment details, and media files. OpenLog does not encrypt this archive. The app first writes it to temporary storage, then saves it to a folder you choose or opens the system share sheet. A file provider or app that you choose can receive a copy. OpenLog does not receive the copy that you save outside the app.

When you share a photo or open an attachment in another app, that app can receive the selected file. The device file picker can also show files from cloud storage providers. Those providers handle the file under their own terms.

Android system backup is enabled. OpenLog's Android rules include shared-preference files and exclude the SQLite database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. Android can copy included preferences to its configured backup or device-transfer service. The code does not identify every value that another library can store in shared preferences.

The app does not configure an iOS backup exclusion. Apple device backups can include app data under your device backup settings. Apple handles those backups under its own policies.

Retention and deletion

OpenLog keeps entries, drafts, and media in app storage until you delete them or the operating system removes the app data. Deleting an entry removes it from the active database and attempts to remove media that no other entry uses. Delete all entries also removes tags, drafts, and unreferenced media. It does not remove your profile name or app preferences.

OpenLog does not promise secure overwriting of deleted database data. Exported backups, files that you share, and copies in system backups remain until you or the service that holds them deletes them. A failed export can leave a temporary archive in app cache.

OpenLog does not set a retention period for PostHog data or website request logs. PostHog and GitHub control those periods through their service settings and policies. The owner must confirm the current periods before publication.

Security

The optional app lock uses the device's biometric or passcode prompt. OpenLog stores the lock setting, not biometric templates or the device passcode. The app lock does not encrypt the timeline database, drafts, media, or backup archives. OpenLog does not add an encryption layer for those files. Protection also depends on your device and operating system settings.

Privacy requests

Your privacy rights depend on where you live. Some laws give you rights to access, correct, delete, or restrict personal information. Email the contact below to ask about a request. OpenLog has no account and does not keep a server copy of your timeline. The owner must confirm how to find and delete PostHog records before publication.

Children and policy changes

The current policy says OpenLog is not directed to children under 13. The app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The owner must confirm the intended age range before publication.

This page shows the current policy date. The app code does not provide an in-app notice for policy changes. The owner must confirm how OpenLog will notify users of material changes.

Contact

The website lists Rwitesh Bera as the maker of OpenLog. For privacy questions, email rwiteshbera@gmail.com. The legal operator name and postal address require confirmation before publication.

# Privacy audit

**Audit date:** 13 November 2026  
**Status:** Static code review. The policy draft needs owner confirmation and legal review before publication.

## Scope and limits

I reviewed app source, configuration, database schemas, permissions, analytics, backup flows, public pages, legal text, and release workflows. I traced data that the app stores, sends, exports, shares, or deletes.

I did not inspect `.env`, remote EAS variables, PostHog project settings, store privacy forms, vendor contracts, or hosting logs. I did not capture live network traffic or test the app on a device or emulator. This report is not a legal opinion.

## Verified data flows

- **Entries and preferences:** SQLite stores entry text, dates, tags, location coordinates and labels, attachment references, the local profile name, and preferences. A full-text index stores entry text and location labels for local search. [Schema](../src/services/db/migrations/v1.ts#L4-L38), [entry storage](../src/services/db/entries.ts#L21-L42), [search index](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L72-L98), and [settings](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L14-L105).
- **Drafts and media:** App document storage holds media files, optional downloaded fonts, and draft files. A draft can contain text, tags, dates, locations, file names, and copies of selected media. [Media storage](../src/services/media/storage.ts#L8-L14), [draft storage](../src/services/drafts/store.ts#L29-L44), and [draft serialization](../src/services/drafts/snapshot.ts#L5-L16).
- **Profile and app lock:** The optional profile name is stored in SQLite. The app stores only an app-lock flag in SecureStore. The OS handles biometric or passcode checks. [Profile storage](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L75-L105), [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56), and [local authentication](../src/services/auth/auth.ts#L19-L41).
- **Permissions:** The app requests photo-library access when a person selects images, microphone access when recording starts, and foreground location after a person selects the location control. Notifications are requested shortly after the timeline opens. [Media picker](../src/modules/compose/hooks/useMediaAttachments.ts#L45-L68), [recording](../src/services/audio/useRecording.ts#L46-L79), [location](../src/services/location/location.ts#L120-L145), and [timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39).
- **Location:** The app passes coordinates to the native reverse-geocoding API after a person asks for a place label. It stores the coordinates and returned label with a draft or entry. It does not request background location. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L145).
- **Analytics:** A build sends PostHog events only when it has a project token and is not in JavaScript development mode. The client uses the US endpoint, captures app lifecycle events, and enables JavaScript exception and unhandled-rejection capture. Interaction autocapture and session replay are off. [PostHog configuration](../src/config/posthog.ts#L1-L25), [screen tracking](../App.tsx#L103-L129), and [event calls](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).
- **Other network requests:** Selecting an optional font downloads a file from jsDelivr. The public website loads Google Fonts. GitHub Pages hosts the website. [Font source](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [website stylesheet](../webpage/style.css#L1), and [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L1-L36).
- **Backups and sharing:** A manual backup contains timeline rows, tags, settings, locations, and referenced media. The app compresses the archive but does not encrypt it. Users choose a folder or share target. [Backup export](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L239) and [export handling](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L109-L187).
- **System backups:** Android Auto Backup is enabled. The rules include shared-preference files and exclude the database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. No iOS backup exclusion appears in the configuration. [Android config](../app.json#L27-L42), [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L8-L38), and [EAS app config](../app.json#L11-L25).
- **Not found:** The tracked app source has no account backend, cloud-sync API, ad SDK, remote push-token registration, or website analytics script. The website source has no cookie code. These findings do not cover hosting-provider behavior or data that users send by email.

## Findings

### F1. High: Analytics disclosure does not match the full data flow

The old policy called analytics anonymous and said it did not collect location. The PostHog SDK creates a persistent pseudonymous identifier and attaches app, device, operating-system, locale, time-zone, and screen details. The app sends `location_used` and `has_location` events, but it does not send GPS coordinates or place labels as event fields. The SDK also exposes the request IP to PostHog. Its IP-based location estimate is not disabled in app configuration. [Old policy](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L3-L23), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry events](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

The app has no analytics opt-out. The production token is not in the repository. EAS selects a remote `production` environment, so this review cannot confirm whether production analytics are active. [EAS profile](../eas.json#L7-L25), [environment template](../.env.example#L1), and [development guide](../DEVELOPMENT.md#L15-L18).

### F2. High: Error reports and launch URLs are not fully scrubbed

The app enables capture of unhandled JavaScript errors and rejected promises. `PostHogErrorBoundary` also sends error details and a component stack. Manual reports replace file paths with `<path>`, but automatic reports do not use that helper. The PostHog lifecycle event can also include the app launch URL. No privacy filter or URL scrubber appears in the app configuration. No content leak was confirmed, but an exception message or URL can contain personal information. [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L11-L19), [error boundary](../App.tsx#L121-L129), and [manual error reporting](../src/shared/utils/devLog.ts#L11-L39).

### F3. High: Local storage, backups, and app lock need clearer limits

The app uses SQLite and app files without an application-level encryption layer. The app lock calls the device authentication prompt, but it does not encrypt entries or attachments. The source also notes that the operating system can take an app-switcher snapshot before the JavaScript cover appears. [Database](../src/services/db/database.ts#L1-L28), [app lock](../src/services/auth/useAppLock.ts#L22-L47), and [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56).

The manual `.openlog` archive is not encrypted. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. Android system backup includes shared preferences, but the repository does not list every value that libraries can store there. iOS app data has no configured backup exclusion. The current policy did not explain these paths. [Export archive](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L132), [export cleanup](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L320-L324), [share fallback](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L137-L171), and [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L12-L38).

### F4. Medium: Location, font, website, and contact requests need disclosure

A location action sends coordinates to the native geocoder. iOS uses Core Location. Android calls the Android Geocoder API, but the repository does not name its downstream provider. The policy did not describe this request. The existing review file already lists this gap as P3-5. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L85) and [open review finding](./review-findings.md#L9-L17).

The app also requests optional fonts from jsDelivr. The website stylesheet requests Google Fonts, and GitHub Pages hosts the site. A person who emails the listed Gmail address sends their message and any attached files to that mailbox. The code does not define retention for website logs or email. [Font resolver](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [site CSS](../webpage/style.css#L1), [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L17-L36), and [contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21).

### F5. Medium: Permission timing and attachment metadata need review

The app requests notification permission shortly after a person first reaches the timeline, not when they start a backup. Local completion notifications can show entry counts and backup size. The iOS configuration declares photo-library write use, but the reviewed app code opens a share sheet and does not call a photo-library write API. The image path can keep the original file, so embedded metadata can remain. [Timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39), [notification content](../src/services/notifications/notifications.ts#L65-L94), [iOS permission string](../app.json#L14-L25), [image path](../src/services/media/images.ts#L11-L48), and [share action](../src/services/media/share.ts#L15-L32).

The attachment picker accepts any file type. It can open selected files in another app. The policy did not describe file-provider or share-target handling. [Document picker](../src/services/media/attachments.ts#L20-L68).

### F6. Medium: Public claims are broader than the implementation

The README says content stays on the device and is never uploaded. The website says the app works offline. The About screen says everything stays on the device. The terms say local content is not uploaded or synced. These statements omit PostHog telemetry, geocoding, font requests, system backups, and user-selected sharing. The old policy also promised practical notice for material changes, but no in-app notice path appears in the app. [README](../README.md#L7-L15), [website](../webpage/index.html#L85-L102), [About screen](../src/screens/settings/AboutSettings.tsx#L79-L84), and [terms](../webpage/terms.html#L27-L38).

The product guide says analytics never include locations. The app sends location-use and location-presence events. These events do not contain exact coordinates, so the guide and event design need a shared definition of location data. [Product guide](../AGENTS.md#L13-L16), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry event fields](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

### F7. Medium: Retention, rights, operator, age, and jurisdiction are unknown

The app sets no local content expiry and has no single control that clears entries, profile details, preferences, font files, and analytics state. Delete-all removes entries, tags, drafts, and unreferenced media, but leaves profile and app preferences. SQLite deletion does not promise secure erasure. PostHog retention, website log retention, and email retention are not defined in the repository. [Delete-all action](../src/modules/entry/store/EntryStore.ts#L139-L147), [privacy settings](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L375-L386), and [database setup](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L33-L50).

The current policy says OpenLog is not directed to children under 13, but the app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The repository names Rwitesh Bera as maker but does not give a legal operator name, postal address, target countries, or privacy-request process. It also does not contain Google Play Data Safety or Apple App Privacy disclosures. [Current policy](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [public contact and terms](../webpage/terms.html#L63-L79), [Android release workflow](../.github/workflows/release-android.yml#L1-L20), and [iOS config](../app.json#L11-L25).

## Recommendations

1. Confirm the production PostHog token, data region, GeoIP behavior, retention, processor terms, subprocessors, and deletion process.
2. Add a user-facing analytics choice or confirm that analytics run by default. Update the policy and store disclosures to match.
3. Disable launch-URL capture unless the app needs it. Add a tested event scrubber for exception text, stack traces, paths, and query values.
4. Decide whether to add encryption for local content and backup archives. Document Android and iOS system-backup behavior. Remove temporary export files on every exit path.
5. Confirm the Android geocoder provider. Keep location use explicit and document that the platform geocoder receives coordinates.
6. Remove the unused photo-library write permission or add and document the feature that needs it. Use the narrowest photo-picker access available. Remove photo metadata before storage or explain that it can remain.
7. Move the notification prompt to a backup action. Limit completion details that appear on lock screens.
8. Self-host website fonts or disclose Google Fonts requests. Document GitHub Pages and contact-mail retention.
9. Align the README, website, About screen, terms, and product guide with the confirmed data flows.
10. Define retention, deletion, and privacy-request steps. Confirm the legal operator, address, age range, user countries, supported platforms, and notice process before publication.

## Owner clarifications

1. Does the production EAS environment contain `EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`? Which release builds send PostHog events?
2. What PostHog region, retention period, GeoIP setting, data-processing terms, and subprocessor list apply? Who handles deletion requests?
3. Does the owner want automatic error capture and launch-URL capture? Will users have an analytics consent or opt-out control?
4. Who is the legal operator and data controller? What legal name, postal address, privacy contact, and email-retention period belong in the policy?
5. Which countries and age groups does OpenLog serve? Is the iOS configuration a released product, and is any web app available?
6. What data can Android shared preferences contain? Does the owner intend Android cloud backup and device transfer? Should iOS backups include app data?
7. Which service resolves Android coordinates? What service terms and retention apply to coordinates sent by the platform geocoder?
8. Does any supported feature save photos directly to the photo library? What rules apply to attachment metadata and files selected from cloud providers?
9. What privacy-request process and notice process does the owner use? Does any business practice share or sell data beyond the flows in this repository?

## Regulatory review

The repository does not establish the operator's country, user countries, age range, or business thresholds. This review cannot decide which laws apply. Counsel must assess the launch markets, including GDPR and UK GDPR, India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, US state privacy laws, and COPPA if the service is directed to children or the owner knows a child under 13 uses it.

Use data minimization, purpose limits, retention limits, and privacy by design as review criteria. Confirm Google Play Data Safety and Apple App Privacy disclosures against the final build. This code review does not establish compliance with any law or security standard.

> Contact

OpenLog / Privacy Policy

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 November 2026 · Draft for legal review

This policy describes how the OpenLog app and website handle information.

Review notice. The code does not show whether production analytics are active, how long PostHog keeps data, which legal entity operates OpenLog, or which age groups and countries OpenLog serves. Resolve the owner questions in docs/privacy-audit.md before publication.

How OpenLog works

OpenLog does not require an account or provide cloud sync. It stores your timeline in app storage on your device. The app does not upload the full timeline to an OpenLog server. Some services receive limited information, as described below.

Information stored on your device

OpenLog stores information that you add or choose:

  • Entry text, dates and times, tags, and locations that you add.
  • Location coordinates and the place label returned by the device geocoder.
  • Photos and voice recordings stored as app files.
  • Other files you attach, plus their names, types, and sizes.
  • Your optional profile name and app preferences.
  • Unsaved drafts, which can include text, media, tags, dates, and locations.

OpenLog uses these data to create, search, and display entries, save drafts, and apply your preferences. Search runs in the local database. The app copies selected media into its local storage.

OpenLog does not remove metadata from every attachment. Some photos stay as original files. They can contain information such as capture time or location.

Analytics and error reports

Some non-development app builds send analytics to PostHog when the build includes the PostHog project token. The code does not show whether the production build includes that token. OpenLog has no in-app control to turn analytics off.

Product events can record:

  • Screen names and app install, update, open, active, and background events.
  • Entry creation, update, or deletion, plus whether an entry has text or a location.
  • Counts of attached photos, recordings, and files.
  • Recording duration, backup entry count, and backup file size.
  • Location use, app-lock changes, and the notification permission choice.

These event fields do not include entry text, media files, attachment names, or exact location coordinates. The app sends a persistent pseudonymous installation identifier. It does not send your profile name or call PostHog's user-identification method.

The PostHog SDK also sends app version and build, device model and manufacturer, operating system and version, locale, time zone, screen size, and the app environment. The PostHog service receives the network request IP address. The app does not disable PostHog's IP-based location estimate, so PostHog can infer an approximate region from that address, subject to project settings. Events go to PostHog's US endpoint.

An app-open event can include the launch URL supplied by the operating system. The SDK also captures unhandled JavaScript errors, rejected promises, and errors from an app error boundary. Error reports can include error messages and stack traces. The app redacts file paths from errors sent through its manual reporting helper. Automatic error reports do not use that helper. An error message or launch URL can contain personal information.

The app disables interaction autocapture, session replay, and console capture. The code does not set a PostHog data-retention period. PostHog's privacy policy and project settings govern its handling and retention.

Location

OpenLog requests foreground location only when you ask to add or refresh a place. It sends the coordinates to the native geocoding service to get a place label. iOS uses Apple's Core Location geocoder. Android uses the Android Geocoder API. The code does not name a fixed downstream provider for Android. These services can receive your coordinates.

OpenLog saves the coordinates and returned place label in the draft or entry on your device. It does not track location in the background. Analytics record whether you used location, not the coordinates or place label.

Fonts and the website

If you select an optional font that is not cached, OpenLog downloads it from the jsDelivr CDN and stores it on your device. The request identifies the font file and sends ordinary network data, such as your IP address. It does not include entry content.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The website stylesheet requests fonts from Google Fonts. GitHub and Google receive website and font requests with ordinary connection data. The website source contains no analytics script or cookie code. The repository does not show the hosting providers' log or cookie practices. Read the GitHub privacy statement and Google Privacy Policy.

The website links to external services. If you open one, that service handles your visit under its own privacy terms.

Permissions and notifications

OpenLog uses these device permissions and pickers:

  • Photo-library access when you choose images to attach.
  • Microphone access when you start a recording.
  • Foreground location access when you ask to add or refresh a place.
  • The system file picker when you choose an attachment or backup.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after the timeline opens. If you allow it, the app creates local notifications for backup and import progress. A completion notice can show the entry count and backup file size. The device can show these notices on its lock screen, subject to your notification settings. The code does not register a remote push-notification token.

Backups and sharing

When you export a backup, OpenLog creates a compressed archive with your entries, tags, settings, locations, attachment details, and media files. OpenLog does not encrypt this archive. The app first writes it to temporary storage, then saves it to a folder you choose or opens the system share sheet. A file provider or app that you choose can receive a copy. OpenLog does not receive the copy that you save outside the app.

When you share a photo or open an attachment in another app, that app can receive the selected file. The device file picker can also show files from cloud storage providers. Those providers handle the file under their own terms.

Android system backup is enabled. OpenLog's Android rules include shared-preference files and exclude the SQLite database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. Android can copy included preferences to its configured backup or device-transfer service. The code does not identify every value that another library can store in shared preferences.

The app does not configure an iOS backup exclusion. Apple device backups can include app data under your device backup settings. Apple handles those backups under its own policies.

Retention and deletion

OpenLog keeps entries, drafts, and media in app storage until you delete them or the operating system removes the app data. Deleting an entry removes it from the active database and attempts to remove media that no other entry uses. Delete all entries also removes tags, drafts, and unreferenced media. It does not remove your profile name or app preferences.

OpenLog does not promise secure overwriting of deleted database data. Exported backups, files that you share, and copies in system backups remain until you or the service that holds them deletes them. A failed export can leave a temporary archive in app cache.

OpenLog does not set a retention period for PostHog data or website request logs. PostHog and GitHub control those periods through their service settings and policies. The owner must confirm the current periods before publication.

Security

The optional app lock uses the device's biometric or passcode prompt. OpenLog stores the lock setting, not biometric templates or the device passcode. The app lock does not encrypt the timeline database, drafts, media, or backup archives. OpenLog does not add an encryption layer for those files. Protection also depends on your device and operating system settings.

Privacy requests

Your privacy rights depend on where you live. Some laws give you rights to access, correct, delete, or restrict personal information. Email the contact below to ask about a request. OpenLog has no account and does not keep a server copy of your timeline. The owner must confirm how to find and delete PostHog records before publication.

Children and policy changes

The current policy says OpenLog is not directed to children under 13. The app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The owner must confirm the intended age range before publication.

This page shows the current policy date. The app code does not provide an in-app notice for policy changes. The owner must confirm how OpenLog will notify users of material changes.

Contact

The website lists Rwitesh Bera as the maker of OpenLog. For privacy questions, email rwiteshbera@gmail.com. If you email us, your address, message, and any files you attach reach that Gmail mailbox. Google handles the email under its privacy policy. The owner must confirm mailbox retention before publication. The legal operator name and postal address also require confirmation.

# Privacy audit

**Audit date:** 13 November 2026  
**Status:** Static code review. The policy draft needs owner confirmation and legal review before publication.

## Scope and limits

I reviewed app source, configuration, database schemas, permissions, analytics, backup flows, public pages, legal text, and release workflows. I traced data that the app stores, sends, exports, shares, or deletes.

I did not inspect `.env`, remote EAS variables, PostHog project settings, store privacy forms, vendor contracts, or hosting logs. I did not capture live network traffic or test the app on a device or emulator. This report is not a legal opinion.

## Verified data flows

- **Entries and preferences:** SQLite stores entry text, dates, tags, location coordinates and labels, attachment references, the local profile name, and preferences. A full-text index stores entry text and location labels for local search. [Schema](../src/services/db/migrations/v1.ts#L4-L38), [entry storage](../src/services/db/entries.ts#L21-L42), [search index](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L72-L98), and [settings](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L14-L105).
- **Drafts and media:** App document storage holds media files, optional downloaded fonts, and draft files. A draft can contain text, tags, dates, locations, file names, and copies of selected media. [Media storage](../src/services/media/storage.ts#L8-L14), [draft storage](../src/services/drafts/store.ts#L29-L44), and [draft serialization](../src/services/drafts/snapshot.ts#L5-L16).
- **Profile and app lock:** The optional profile name is stored in SQLite. The app stores only an app-lock flag in SecureStore. The OS handles biometric or passcode checks. [Profile storage](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L75-L105), [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56), and [local authentication](../src/services/auth/auth.ts#L19-L41).
- **Permissions:** The app requests photo-library access when a person selects images, microphone access when recording starts, and foreground location after a person selects the location control. Notifications are requested shortly after the timeline opens. ## Findings

### F1. High: Analytics disclosure does not match the full data flow

The old policy called analytics anonymous and said it did not collect location. The PostHog SDK creates a persistent pseudonymous identifier and attaches app, device, operating-system, locale, time-zone, and screen details. The app sends `location_used` and `has_location` events, but it does not send GPS coordinates or place labels as event fields. The SDK also exposes the request IP to PostHog. Its IP-based location estimate is not disabled in app configuration. [Old policy](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L3-L23), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry events](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

The app has no analytics opt-out. The production token is not in the repository. EAS selects a remote `production` environment, so this review cannot confirm whether production analytics are active. ### F2. High: Error reports and launch URLs are not fully scrubbed

The app enables capture of unhandled JavaScript errors and rejected promises. `PostHogErrorBoundary` also sends error details and a component stack. Manual reports replace file paths with `<path>`, but automatic reports do not use that helper. The PostHog lifecycle event can also include the app launch URL. No privacy filter or URL scrubber appears in the app configuration. No content leak was confirmed, but an exception message or URL can contain personal information. [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L11-L19), [error boundary](../App.tsx#L121-L129), and [manual error reporting](../src/shared/utils/devLog.ts#L11-L39).

### F3. High: Local storage, backups, and app lock need clearer limits

The app uses SQLite and app files without an application-level encryption layer. The app lock calls the device authentication prompt, but it does not encrypt entries or attachments. The source also notes that the operating system can take an app-switcher snapshot before the JavaScript cover appears. [Database](../src/services/db/database.ts#L1-L28), [app lock](../src/services/auth/useAppLock.ts#L22-L47), and [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56).

The manual `.openlog` archive is not encrypted. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. Android system backup includes shared preferences, but the repository does not list every value that libraries can store there. iOS app data has no configured backup exclusion. The current policy did not explain these paths. [Export archive](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L132), [export cleanup](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L320-L324), [share fallback](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L137-L171), and [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L12-L38).

### F4. Medium: Location, font, website, and contact requests need disclosure

A location action sends coordinates to the native geocoder. iOS uses Core Location. Android calls the Android Geocoder API, but the repository does not name its downstream provider. The policy did not describe this request. The existing review file already lists this gap as P3-5. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L85) and [open review finding](./review-findings.md#L9-L17).

The app also requests optional fonts from jsDelivr. The website stylesheet requests Google Fonts, and GitHub Pages hosts the site. The app requests notification permission shortly after the timeline opens, not when a person starts a backup. Local completion notifications can show entry counts and backup size. The app sets no local content expiry and has no single control that clears entries, profile details, preferences, font files, and analytics state. ## Recommendations

1. Confirm the production PostHog token, data region, GeoIP behavior, retention, processor terms, subprocessors, and deletion process.
2. Add a user-facing analytics choice or confirm that analytics run by default. Update the policy and store disclosures to match.
3. Disable launch-URL capture unless the app needs it. Add a tested event scrubber for exception text, stack traces, paths, and query values.
4. Decide whether to add encryption for local content and backup archives. Document Android and iOS system-backup behavior. Remove temporary export files on every exit path.
5. Confirm the Android geocoder provider. Keep location use explicit and document that the platform geocoder receives coordinates.
6. Remove the unused photo-library write permission or add and document the feature that needs it. Use the narrowest photo-picker access available. Remove photo metadata before storage or explain that it can remain.
7. Move the notification prompt to a backup action. Limit completion details that appear on lock screens.
8. Self-host website fonts or disclose Google Fonts requests. Document GitHub Pages and contact-mail retention.
9. Align the README, website, About screen, terms, and product guide with the confirmed data flows.
10. Define retention, deletion, and privacy-request steps. Confirm the legal operator, address, age range, user countries, supported platforms, and notice process before publication.

The repository does not establish the operator's country, user countries, age range, or business thresholds. This review cannot decide which laws apply. Counsel must assess the launch markets. Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 November 2026 · Draft for legal review

This policy describes how the OpenLog app and website handle information.

Review notice. The code does not show whether production analytics are active, how long PostHog keeps data, which legal entity operates OpenLog, or which age groups and countries OpenLog serves. Resolve the owner questions in the audit report before publication.

How OpenLog works

OpenLog does not require an account or provide cloud sync. It stores your timeline in app storage on your device. The app does not upload the full timeline to an OpenLog server. Some services receive limited information, as described below.

Information stored on your device

OpenLog stores information that you add or choose:

  • Entry text, dates and times, tags, and locations that you add.
  • Location coordinates and the place label returned by the device geocoder.
  • Photos and voice recordings stored as app files.
  • Other files you attach, plus their names, types, and sizes.
  • Your optional profile name and app preferences.
  • Unsaved drafts, which can include text, media, tags, dates, and locations.

OpenLog uses these data to create, search, and display entries, save drafts, and apply your preferences. Search runs in the local database. The app copies selected media into its local storage.

OpenLog does not remove metadata from every attachment. Some photos stay as original files. They can contain information such as capture time or location.

Analytics and error reports

Some non-development app builds send analytics to PostHog when the build includes the PostHog project token. The code does not show whether the production build includes that token. OpenLog has no in-app control to turn analytics off.

Product events can record:

  • Screen names and app install, update, open, active, and background events.
  • Entry creation, update, or deletion, plus whether an entry has text or a location.
  • Counts of attached photos, recordings, and files.
  • Recording duration, backup entry count, and backup file size.
  • Location use, app-lock changes, and the notification permission choice.

These event fields do not include entry text, media files, attachment names, or exact location coordinates. The app sends a persistent pseudonymous installation identifier. The SDK stores this identifier and pending events in app storage. The app does not set an expiry for the event queue. It does not send your profile name or call PostHog's user-identification method.

The PostHog SDK also sends the app identifier, version, build, and environment. It sends device model and manufacturer, operating system and version, locale, time zone, and screen size. The PostHog service receives the network request IP address. The app does not disable PostHog's IP-based location estimate, so PostHog can infer an approximate region from that address, subject to project settings. Events go to PostHog's US endpoint. OpenLog uses these events for product analytics and error diagnosis.

An app-open event can include the launch URL supplied by the operating system. The SDK also captures unhandled JavaScript errors, rejected promises, and errors from an app error boundary. Error reports can include error messages and stack traces. The app redacts file paths from errors sent through its manual reporting helper. Automatic error reports do not use that helper. An error message or launch URL can contain personal information.

The app disables interaction autocapture, session replay, and console capture. The code does not set a PostHog data-retention period. PostHog's privacy policy and project settings govern its handling and retention.

Location

OpenLog requests foreground location only when you ask to add or refresh a place. It sends the coordinates to the native geocoding service to get a place label. iOS uses Apple's Core Location geocoder. Android uses the Android Geocoder API. The code does not name a fixed downstream provider for Android. These services can receive your coordinates.

OpenLog saves the coordinates and returned place label in the draft or entry on your device. It does not track location in the background. Analytics record whether you used location, not the coordinates or place label.

Fonts and the website

If you select an optional font that is not cached, OpenLog downloads it from the jsDelivr CDN and stores it on your device. The request identifies the font file and sends ordinary network data, such as your IP address. It does not include entry content. The app keeps downloaded fonts until you remove them or the operating system removes app data.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The website stylesheet requests fonts from Google Fonts. GitHub and Google receive website and font requests with ordinary connection data. The website source contains no analytics script or cookie code. The repository does not show the hosting providers' log or cookie practices. Read the GitHub privacy statement and Google Privacy Policy.

The website links to external services. If you open one, that service handles your visit under its own privacy terms.

Permissions and notifications

OpenLog uses these device permissions and pickers:

  • Photo-library access when you choose images to attach.
  • Microphone access when you start a recording.
  • Foreground location access when you ask to add or refresh a place.
  • The system file picker when you choose an attachment or backup.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after the timeline opens. If you allow it, the app creates local notifications for backup and import progress. A completion notice can show the entry count and backup file size. The device can show these notices on its lock screen, subject to your notification settings. The code does not register a remote push-notification token.

Backups and sharing

When you export a backup, OpenLog creates a compressed archive with your entries, tags, app settings, profile name, locations, attachment details, and media files. OpenLog does not encrypt this archive. The app first writes it to temporary storage, then saves it to a folder you choose or opens the system share sheet. A file provider or app that you choose can receive a copy. OpenLog does not receive the copy that you save outside the app.

When you share a photo or open an attachment in another app, that app can receive the selected file. The device file picker can also show files from cloud storage providers. Those providers handle the file under their own terms.

Android system backup is enabled. OpenLog's Android rules include shared-preference files and exclude the SQLite database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. Android can copy included preferences to its configured backup or device-transfer service. The code does not identify every value that another library can store in shared preferences.

The app does not configure an iOS backup exclusion. Apple device backups can include app data under your device backup settings. Apple handles those backups under its own policies.

Retention and deletion

Unsaved drafts remain until you save or discard them. Saved entries and media remain in app storage until you delete them or the operating system removes the app data. Deleting an entry removes it from the active database and attempts to remove media that no other entry uses. Delete all entries also removes tags, drafts, and unreferenced media. It does not remove your profile name or app preferences.

OpenLog does not promise secure overwriting of deleted database data. Exported backups, files that you share, and copies in system backups remain until you or the service that holds them deletes them. A failed export can leave a temporary archive in app cache.

OpenLog does not set a retention period for PostHog data or website request logs. PostHog and GitHub control those periods through their service settings and policies. The owner must confirm the current periods before publication.

Security

The optional app lock uses the device's biometric or passcode prompt. OpenLog stores the lock setting, not biometric templates or the device passcode. The app lock does not encrypt the timeline database, drafts, media, or backup archives. OpenLog does not add an encryption layer for those files. Protection also depends on your device and operating system settings.

Privacy requests

Your privacy rights depend on where you live. Some laws give you rights to access, correct, delete, or restrict personal information. Email the contact below to ask about a request. OpenLog has no account and does not keep a server copy of your timeline. The owner must confirm how to find and delete PostHog records before publication.

Children and policy changes

The previously published policy said OpenLog is not directed to children under 13. The app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The owner must confirm the intended age range before publication.

This page shows the current policy date. The app code does not provide an in-app notice for policy changes. The owner must confirm how OpenLog will notify users of material changes.

Contact

The website lists Rwitesh Bera as the maker of OpenLog. For privacy questions, email rwiteshbera@gmail.com. If you email us, your address, message, and any files you attach reach that Gmail mailbox. OpenLog uses the message to answer your request. Google handles the email under its privacy policy. The owner must confirm mailbox retention before publication. The legal operator name and postal address also require confirmation.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 November 2026 · Draft for legal review

This policy describes how the OpenLog app and website handle information.

Review notice. The code does not show whether production analytics are active, how long PostHog keeps data, which legal entity operates OpenLog, or which age groups and countries OpenLog serves. Resolve the owner questions in the audit report before publication.

How OpenLog works

OpenLog does not require an account or provide cloud sync. It stores your timeline in app storage on your device. The app does not upload the full timeline to an OpenLog server. Some services receive limited information, as described below.

Information stored on your device

OpenLog stores information that you add or choose:

  • Entry text, dates and times, tags, and locations that you add.
  • Location coordinates and the place label returned by the device geocoder.
  • Photos and voice recordings stored as app files.
  • Other files you attach, plus their names, types, and sizes.
  • Your optional profile name and app preferences.
  • Unsaved drafts, which can include text, media, tags, dates, and locations.

OpenLog uses these data to create, search, and display entries, save drafts, and apply your preferences. Search runs in the local database. The app copies selected media into its local storage.

OpenLog does not remove metadata from every attachment. Some photos stay as original files. They can contain information such as capture time or location.

Analytics and error reports

Some non-development app builds send analytics to PostHog when the build includes the PostHog project token. The code does not show whether the production build includes that token. OpenLog has no in-app control to turn analytics off.

Product events can record:

  • Screen names and app install, update, open, active, and background events.
  • Entry creation, update, or deletion, plus whether an entry has text or a location.
  • Counts of attached photos, recordings, and files.
  • Recording duration, backup entry count, and backup file size.
  • Location use, app-lock changes, and the notification permission choice.

These event fields do not include entry text, media files, attachment names, or exact location coordinates. The app sends a persistent installation ID that does not contain your name. PostHog can use this ID to link events from the same installation. The SDK stores the ID and pending events in app storage. The app does not set an expiry for the event queue. The app does not add your profile name or email address to product-event fields.

The PostHog SDK also sends the app identifier, version, build, and environment. It sends device model and manufacturer, operating system and version, locale, time zone, and screen size. PostHog receives the network request IP address. The app leaves PostHog's IP-based location estimate on. PostHog can infer an approximate region from that address, subject to project configuration. Events go to PostHog's US endpoint. OpenLog uses these events for product analytics and error diagnosis.

An app-open event can include the launch URL supplied by the operating system. The SDK also captures unhandled JavaScript errors, rejected promises, and errors from an app error boundary. Error reports can include error messages and stack traces. The app redacts file paths from errors sent through its manual reporting helper. Automatic error reports do not use that helper. An error message or launch URL can contain personal information.

The app does not record session replay, capture taps automatically, or collect console logs. The code does not set a PostHog data-retention period. PostHog's privacy policy and project settings govern its handling and retention.

Location

OpenLog requests foreground location only when you ask to add or refresh a place. It sends the coordinates to the native geocoding service to get a place label. iOS uses Apple's Core Location geocoder. Android uses the Android Geocoder API. The code does not name a fixed downstream provider for Android. These services can receive your coordinates.

OpenLog saves the coordinates and returned place label in the draft or entry on your device. It does not track location in the background. Analytics record whether you used location, not the coordinates or place label.

Fonts and the website

If you select an optional font that is not cached, OpenLog downloads it from the jsDelivr CDN and stores it on your device. The request identifies the font file and sends ordinary network data, such as your IP address. It does not include entry content. The app keeps downloaded fonts until you remove them or the operating system removes app data.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The website stylesheet requests fonts from Google Fonts. GitHub and Google receive website and font requests with ordinary connection data. The native app does not use browser cookies. The website source contains no analytics script or cookie code. The repository does not show the hosting providers' log or cookie practices. Read the GitHub privacy statement and Google Privacy Policy.

The website links to external services. If you open one, that service handles your visit under its own privacy terms.

Permissions and notifications

OpenLog uses these device permissions and pickers:

  • Photo-library access when you choose images to attach.
  • Microphone access when you start a recording.
  • Foreground location access when you ask to add or refresh a place.
  • The system file picker when you choose an attachment or backup.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after the timeline opens. If you allow it, the app creates local notifications for backup and import progress. A completion notice can show the entry count and backup file size. The device can show these notices on its lock screen, subject to your notification settings. The code does not register a remote push-notification token.

Backups and sharing

When you export a backup, OpenLog creates a compressed archive with your entries, tags, app settings, profile name, locations, attachment details, and media files. OpenLog does not encrypt this archive. The app first writes it to temporary storage, then saves it to a folder you choose or opens the system share sheet. A file provider or app that you choose can receive a copy. OpenLog does not receive the copy that you save outside the app.

When you share a photo or open an attachment in another app, that app can receive the selected file. The device file picker can also show files from cloud storage providers. Those providers handle the file under their own terms.

Android system backup is enabled. OpenLog's Android rules include shared-preference files and exclude the SQLite database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. Android can copy included preferences to its configured backup or device-transfer service. The code does not identify every value that another library can store in shared preferences.

The app does not configure an iOS backup exclusion. Apple device backups can include app data under your device backup settings. Apple handles those backups under its own policies.

Retention and deletion

Unsaved drafts remain until you save or discard them. Saved entries and media remain in app storage until you delete them or the operating system removes the app data. Deleting an entry removes it from the active database and attempts to remove media that no other entry uses. Delete all entries also removes tags, drafts, and unreferenced media. It does not remove your profile name or app preferences.

OpenLog does not promise secure overwriting of deleted database data. Exported backups, files that you share, and copies in system backups remain until you or the service that holds them deletes them. A failed export can leave a temporary archive in app cache.

OpenLog does not set a retention period for PostHog data or website request logs. PostHog and GitHub control those periods through their service settings and policies. The owner must confirm the current periods before publication.

Security

The optional app lock uses the device's biometric or passcode prompt. OpenLog stores the lock setting, not biometric templates or the device passcode. The app lock does not encrypt the timeline database, drafts, media, or backup archives. OpenLog does not add an encryption layer for those files. Protection also depends on your device and operating system settings.

Privacy requests

Your privacy rights depend on where you live. Some laws give you rights to access, correct, delete, or restrict personal information. Email the contact below to ask about a request. OpenLog has no account and does not keep a server copy of your timeline. The owner must confirm how to find and delete PostHog records before publication.

Children and policy changes

The previously published policy said OpenLog is not directed to children under 13. The app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The owner must confirm the intended age range before publication.

This page shows the current policy date. The app code does not provide an in-app notice for policy changes. The owner must confirm how OpenLog will notify users of material changes.

Contact

The website lists Rwitesh Bera as the maker of OpenLog. For privacy questions, email rwiteshbera@gmail.com. If you email us, your address, message, and any files you attach reach that Gmail mailbox. OpenLog uses the message to answer your request. Google handles the email under its privacy policy. The owner must confirm mailbox retention before publication. The owner must also add the legal operator name and postal address before publication.

# Privacy audit

**Audit date:** 13 November 2026  
**Status:** Static code review. The policy draft needs owner confirmation and legal review before publication.

## Scope and limits

I reviewed app source, configuration, database schemas, permissions, analytics, backup flows, public pages, legal text, and release workflows. I traced data that the app stores, sends, exports, shares, or deletes.

I did not inspect `.env`, remote EAS variables, PostHog project configuration, store privacy forms, vendor contracts, or hosting logs. I did not capture live network traffic or test the app on a device or emulator. This report is not a legal opinion.

## Confirmed data flows

- **Entries and preferences:** SQLite stores entry text, dates, tags, location coordinates and labels, attachment references, the local profile name, and preferences. A full-text index stores entry text and location labels for local search. [Schema](../src/services/db/migrations/v1.ts#L4-L38), [entry storage](../src/services/db/entries.ts#L21-L42), [search index](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L72-L98), and [preference storage](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L14-L105).
- **Drafts and media:** App document storage holds media files, optional downloaded fonts, and draft files. A draft can contain text, tags, dates, locations, file names, and copies of selected media. [Media storage](../src/services/media/storage.ts#L8-L14), [draft storage](../src/services/drafts/store.ts#L29-L44), and [draft serialization](../src/services/drafts/snapshot.ts#L5-L16).
- **Profile and app lock:** The optional profile name is stored in SQLite. The app stores only an app-lock flag in SecureStore. The OS handles biometric or passcode checks. [Profile storage](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L75-L105), [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56), and [local authentication](../src/services/auth/auth.ts#L19-L41).
- **Permissions:** The app requests photo-library access when a person selects images. It requests microphone access when recording starts. It requests foreground location after a person selects the location control. Notifications are requested shortly after the timeline opens. [Media picker](../src/modules/compose/hooks/useMediaAttachments.ts#L45-L68), [recording](../src/services/audio/useRecording.ts#L46-L79), [location](../src/services/location/location.ts#L120-L145), and [timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39).
- **Location:** The app passes coordinates to the native reverse-geocoding API after a person asks for a place label. It stores the coordinates and returned label with a draft or entry. It does not request background location. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L145).
- **Analytics:** A build sends PostHog events only when it has a project token and is not in JavaScript development mode. The client uses the US endpoint, captures app lifecycle events, and enables JavaScript exception and unhandled-rejection capture. Interaction autocapture and session replay are off. [PostHog configuration](../src/config/posthog.ts#L1-L25), [screen tracking](../App.tsx#L103-L129), and [event calls](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).
- **Other network requests:** Selecting an optional font downloads a file from jsDelivr. The public website loads Google Fonts. GitHub Pages hosts the website. [Font source](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [website stylesheet](../webpage/style.css#L1), and [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L1-L36).
- **Build and distribution:** GitHub Actions requests Android builds from EAS and uploads them to Google Play. The workflow has no path to runtime entries. Store-side data collection was not reviewed. [Android release workflow](../.github/workflows/release-android.yml#L74-L121).
- **Backups and sharing:** A manual backup contains timeline rows, tags, preferences, locations, and referenced media. The app compresses the archive but does not encrypt it. Users choose a folder or share target. [Backup export](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L239) and [export handling](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L109-L187).
- **System backups:** Android Auto Backup is enabled. The rules include shared-preference files and exclude the database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. No iOS backup exclusion appears in the configuration. [Android app declaration](../app.json#L27-L42), [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L8-L38), and [EAS app declaration](../app.json#L11-L25).
- **Not found:** The tracked app source has no account backend, cloud-sync API, ad SDK, remote push-token registration, or website analytics script. The website source has no cookie code. [Dependencies](../package.json#L1-L43) and [website home page](../webpage/index.html#L1-L116). These findings do not cover hosting-provider behavior or data that users send by email.

## Findings

### F1. High: Analytics disclosure does not match the full data flow

The version of `webpage/privacy-policy.html` on `main` called analytics anonymous and said it did not collect location. This draft replaces those claims. The PostHog SDK creates a persistent pseudonymous identifier and attaches app, device, operating-system, locale, time-zone, and screen details. The app sends `location_used` and `has_location` events, but it does not send GPS coordinates or place labels as event fields. The SDK also exposes the request IP to PostHog. Its IP-based location estimate is not disabled in app configuration. [Current policy draft](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L3-L23), [locked SDK version](../pnpm-lock.yaml#L2321-L2332), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry events](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

The app has no analytics opt-out. The privacy screen contains app lock, backup, and storage controls only. The production token is not in the repository. EAS selects a remote `production` environment, so this review cannot confirm whether production analytics are active. [Privacy screen](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L389-L464), [EAS profile](../eas.json#L7-L25), [environment template](../.env.example#L1), and [development guide](../DEVELOPMENT.md#L15-L18).

### F2. High: Error reports and launch URLs are not fully scrubbed

The app enables capture of unhandled JavaScript errors and rejected promises. `PostHogErrorBoundary` also sends error details and a component stack. Manual reports replace file paths with `<path>`, but automatic reports do not use that helper. The PostHog lifecycle event can also include the app launch URL. No global filter or launch-URL scrubber appears in the app configuration. No content leak was confirmed, but an exception message or URL can contain personal information. [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L11-L19), [error boundary](../App.tsx#L121-L129), [app scheme](../app.json#L5-L12), [locked SDK version](../pnpm-lock.yaml#L2321-L2332), and [manual error reporting](../src/shared/utils/devLog.ts#L11-L39).

### F3. High: Local storage, backups, and app lock need clearer limits

The app uses SQLite and app files without an application-level encryption layer. The app lock calls the device authentication prompt, but it does not encrypt entries or attachments. The source also notes that the operating system can take an app-switcher snapshot before the JavaScript cover appears. [Database](../src/services/db/database.ts#L1-L28), [app lock](../src/services/auth/useAppLock.ts#L22-L47), and [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56).

The manual `.openlog` archive is not encrypted. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. Android system backup includes shared preferences, but the repository does not list every value that libraries can store there. iOS app data has no configured backup exclusion. The current policy did not explain these paths. ### F4. Medium: Location, font, website, and contact requests need disclosure

A location action sends coordinates to the native geocoder. iOS uses Core Location. Android calls the Android Geocoder API, but the repository does not name its downstream provider. The policy did not describe this request. The existing review file already lists this gap as P3-5. The app also requests optional fonts from jsDelivr. The website stylesheet requests Google Fonts, and GitHub Pages hosts the site. A person who emails the listed Gmail address sends their message and any attached files to that mailbox. The code does not define retention for website logs or email. ### F5. Medium: Permission timing and attachment metadata need review

The app requests notification permission shortly after the timeline opens, not when a person starts a backup. Local completion notifications can show entry counts and backup size. The iOS configuration declares photo-library write use, but the reviewed app code opens a share sheet and does not call a photo-library write API. The image path can keep the original file, so embedded metadata can remain. The attachment picker accepts any file type. It can open selected files in another app. The policy did not describe file-provider or share-target handling. [Document picker](../src/services/media/attachments.ts#L20-L68).

The privacy contact uses a Gmail address. The code does not define mailbox-provider retention or how the owner handles requests. [Contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21).

The README says content stays on the device and is never uploaded. The website says the app works offline. The About screen says everything stays on the device. The terms say local content is not uploaded or synced. These statements omit PostHog telemetry, geocoding, font requests, system backups, and user-selected sharing. The product guide says analytics never include locations. The app sends location-use and location-presence events. The app sets no local content expiry and has no single control that clears entries, profile details, preferences, font files, and analytics state. Delete-all removes entries, tags, drafts, and unreferenced media, but leaves profile and app preferences. SQLite deletion does not promise secure erasure. The previous policy said OpenLog is not directed to children under 13, but the app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The repository names Rwitesh Bera as maker but does not give a legal operator name, postal address, target countries, or privacy-request process. [Policy draft](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [public contact and terms](../webpage/terms.html#L63-L79), [Android release workflow](../.github/workflows/release-android.yml#L1-L20), and [iOS config](../app.json#L11-L25).

## Recommendations

1. Confirm the production PostHog token, data region, GeoIP behavior, retention, processor terms, subprocessors, and deletion process.
2. Add a user-facing analytics choice or confirm that analytics run by default. Update the policy and store disclosures to match.
3. Disable launch-URL capture unless the app needs it. Add a tested event scrubber for exception text, stack traces, paths, and query values.
4. Decide whether to add encryption for local content and backup archives. Document Android and iOS system-backup behavior. Remove temporary export files on every exit path.
5. Confirm the Android geocoder provider. Keep location use explicit and document that the platform geocoder receives coordinates.
6. Remove the unused photo-library write permission or add and document the feature that needs it. Use the narrowest photo-picker access available. Remove photo metadata before storage or explain that it can remain.
7. Move the notification prompt to a backup action. Limit completion details that appear on lock screens.
8. Self-host website fonts or disclose Google Fonts requests. Document GitHub Pages and contact-mail retention.
9. Align the README, website, About screen, terms, and product guide with the confirmed data flows.
10. Define retention, deletion, and privacy-request steps. Confirm the legal operator, address, age range, user countries, supported platforms, and notice process before publication.

## Owner clarifications

1. Does the production EAS environment contain `EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`? Which release builds send PostHog events?
2. What PostHog region, retention period, GeoIP configuration, data-processing terms, and subprocessor list apply? Who handles deletion requests?
3. Does the owner want automatic error and launch-URL capture? What legal basis and user choice apply to analytics and location requests in each market?
4. Who is the legal operator and data controller? What legal name, postal address, privacy contact, and email-retention period belong in the policy?
5. Which countries and age groups does OpenLog serve? Is the iOS configuration a released product, and is any web app available?
6. What data can Android shared preferences contain? Does the owner intend Android cloud backup and device transfer? Does the owner want iOS backups to include app data?
7. Which service resolves Android coordinates? What service terms and retention apply to coordinates sent by the platform geocoder?
8. Does any supported feature save photos directly to the photo library? What rules apply to attachment metadata and files selected from cloud providers?
9. What privacy-request process and notice process does the owner use? Does any business practice share or sell data beyond the flows in this repository?

## Regulatory review

The repository does not establish the country of the operator, user countries, age range, or business thresholds. This review cannot decide which laws apply. Counsel must assess the launch markets. Candidate laws include GDPR, UK GDPR, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act of India, US state privacy laws, and COPPA. Counsel must assess COPPA if the service targets children or the owner knows a child under 13 uses it.

Use data minimization, purpose limits, retention limits, and privacy by design as review criteria. Confirm Google Play Data Safety and Apple App Privacy disclosures against the final build. This code review does not establish compliance with any law or security standard.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The website stylesheet requests fonts from Google Fonts. GitHub and Google receive website and font requests with ordinary connection data. The native app does not use browser cookies. The website source contains no analytics script or cookie code. The repository does not show the hosting providers' log or cookie practices. Read the GitHub privacy statement and Google Privacy Policy.

The website links to external services. If you open one, that service handles your visit under its own privacy terms.

Permissions and notifications

OpenLog uses these device permissions and pickers:

  • Photo-library access when you choose images to attach.
  • Microphone access when you start a recording.
  • Foreground location access when you ask to add or refresh a place.
  • The system file picker when you choose an attachment or backup.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after the timeline opens. If you allow it, the app creates local notifications for backup and import progress. A completion notice can show the entry count and backup file size. The device can show these notices on its lock screen, subject to your notification settings. The code does not register a remote push-notification token.

Backups and sharing

When you export a backup, OpenLog creates a compressed archive with your entries, tags, app settings, profile name, locations, attachment details, and media files. OpenLog does not encrypt this archive. The app first writes it to temporary storage, then saves it to a folder you choose or opens the system share sheet. A file provider or app that you choose can receive a copy. OpenLog does not receive the copy that you save outside the app.

When you share a photo or open an attachment in another app, that app can receive the selected file. The device file picker can also show files from cloud storage providers. Those providers handle the file under their own terms.

Android system backup is enabled. OpenLog's Android rules include shared-preference files and exclude the SQLite database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. Android can copy included preferences to its configured backup or device-transfer service. The code does not identify every value that another library can store in shared preferences.

Create a pull request on GitHub.

Upon success, the URL of the created pull request will be printed.

When the current branch isn't fully pushed to a git remote, a prompt will ask where
to push the branch and offer an option to fork the base repository. Any fork created this
way will only have the default branch of the upstream repository. Use `--head` to
explicitly skip any forking or pushing behavior.

`--head` supports `<user>:<branch>` syntax to select a head repo owned by `<user>`.
Using an organization as the `<user>` is currently not supported.
For more information, see <https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/10093>

A prompt will also ask for the title and the body of the pull request. Use `--title` and
`--body` to skip this, or use `--fill` to autofill these values from git commits.
It's important to notice that if the `--title` and/or `--body` are also provided
alongside `--fill`, the values specified by `--title` and/or `--body` will
take precedence and overwrite any autofilled content.

The base branch for the created PR can be specified using the `--base` flag. If not provided,
the value of `gh-merge-base` git branch config will be used. If not configured, the repository's
default branch will be used. Run `git config branch.{current}.gh-merge-base {base}` to configure
the current branch to use the specified merge base.

Link an issue to the pull request by referencing the issue in the body of the pull
request. If the body text mentions `Fixes #123` or `Closes #123`, the referenced issue
will automatically get closed when the pull request gets merged.

Use `--attach` to upload an image or video. The attachment is appended to the
body. If the body references an attached file, such as `![alt](./login.png)`, that
reference is rewritten to point at the uploaded asset instead. Paths in a
`--body-file` are relative to its directory, falling back to the working directory.
You can attach up to 50 files per command.

Alt text for an image follows the path after `#`, as in
`--attach './login.png#The login error state'`. Without it the filename is used.
A reference already in the body keeps the alt text written there. Video renders
as a player and has no alt text, so it cannot be given any.

If some attachments upload and others fail, the pull request is still created with the
ones that succeeded. The command then exits with a non-zero status, but the new pull
request's URL is still printed to stdout.

By default, users with write access to the base repository can push new commits to the
head branch of the pull request. Disable this with `--no-maintainer-edit`.

Adding a pull request to projects requires authorization with the `project` scope.
To authorize, run `gh auth refresh -s project`.
